handbookNote: Utah Motorcycle Operator Manual (18th Ed. MSF base manual, June 2020 revision, with a Utah-specific insert authored by the Utah Driver License Division, DLD), fetched fresh this session from the official direct PDF link dld.utah.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024-Motorcycle-Handbook.pdf, linked from the official Motorcycle Handbook page dld.utah.gov/motorcycle-handbook/ and the Motorcycle Endorsement page dld.utah.gov/add-motorcycle-endorsement/. Full text was extracted directly from this PDF via pdftotext and used as the sole grounding source for every question, including the manual's 22-page Utah-specific insert (pages UT1-UT22: required equipment, helmet law, tiered licensing, learner permit rules, lane filtering, traffic rules, OHV/ATV Type I and II, moped/e-bike/motor-assisted-scooter/mini-motorcycle/autocycle definitions, and the Utah Rider Training Program's BRC/BRC2 courses) and its full Three-Wheel Motorcycle Supplement chapter -- the same agency (Utah DLD, a division of the Department of Public Safety, distinct from the vehicle-registration DMV) that publishes this project's existing ut_driver and ut_cdl tracks. Price matches this project's established Motorcycle tier ($7.99), not a placeholder. EXAM MECHANICS PARTIALLY CONFIRMED, PARTIALLY HEDGED, same pattern as ut_driver and ut_cdl: CONFIRMED directly from two independent official dld.utah.gov pages (dld.utah.gov/add-motorcycle-endorsement/ and dld.utah.gov/motorcycle/, both fetched this session) -- the Utah motorcycle endorsement written knowledge test is 'a 25-question closed-book test,' and applicants must be at least 16 years old and hold a valid Class D driver license. Utah's motorcycle learner permit requires passing this test plus a vision test, is valid six months, and carries first-two-month restrictions (no highway riding at 60+ mph, no passengers, no riding 10pm-6am) waivable for under-19 applicants who complete the Basic Rider Course. Utah's tiered endorsement system restricts riders to the engine-size class (90cc/249cc/649cc/650cc-plus/three-wheel) of the motorcycle used on their skills test. HEDGED: neither dld.utah.gov page states a passing-score percentage for the motorcycle test specifically (confirmed absent by exhaustive review of both pages and the manual's own 'Earning Your License' section, which describes the knowledge-test format generically without a numeric passing standard). This project's ut_driver track separately confirmed Utah's general driver knowledge test passing standard is 80% (per the Driver Handbook's Section 6 and dld.utah.gov/written-knowledge-test/); third-party test-prep aggregators (driving-tests.org, zutobi.com, dmv-written-test.com, dmv-permit-test.com) consistently report the motorcycle test also requires 20 of 25 correct (80%), consistent with Utah's general standard, but this specific figure is NOT stated verbatim on either official motorcycle-specific DLD page and must be treated as well-corroborated, not government-confirmed-verbatim for the motorcycle test, in any EXAM_CONFIGS code comment at wiring time. Content-depth rationale: the manual combines the standard 18th-edition MSF body (gear, vehicle control, braking/ABS, lane position and following distance, SEE strategy, intersections, conspicuity, crash avoidance, dangerous surfaces, mechanical problems, animals, passengers/cargo, group riding, alcohol/drugs/fatigue, licensing) with an unusually rich 22-page Utah-specific statutory insert covering not just motorcycles but street-legal ATVs, mopeds, e-bikes, motor-assisted scooters, mini-motorcycles, and autocycles -- content not present in most other states' motorcycle manuals -- plus a full three-wheel motorcycle and sidecar supplement, comfortably supporting a large, non-repetitive bank. 205 questions across 16 topic buckets survived the build pipeline's structural and dedup checks; every question is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched manual text or one of the two confirmed dld.utah.gov pages cited in its source_note, with no fact carried over from any other state's build. Answer-choice letters were rebalanced with a deterministic round-robin rotation script (choice_a drafted correct first, then rotated into A/B/C/D by global running order) rather than chosen manually, yielding a final bank-wide distribution of A=25.4% / B=24.9% / C=24.9% / D=24.9%, all within the required 15-35% band per letter.
